arxiv-1506-04452.title: Modeling the Association Structure in Doubly Robust GEE for Longitudinal Ordinal Missing Data
arxiv-1506-04452.creator: José Luiz P. da Silva, Enrico A. Colosimo, Fábio N. Demarqui
arxiv-1506-04452.description: Abstract Generalized Estimation Equations (GEE) are a well-known method for the analysis of categorical longitudinal responses. GEE method has computational simplicity and population parameter interpretation. In the presence of missing data it is only valid under the strong assumption of missing completely at random.

arxiv-2103-08575.title: Nowhere to Hide: Radio-faint AGN in the GOODS-N field
arxiv-2103-08575.creator: J. F. Radcliffe, P. D. Barthel, A. P. Thomson, M. A. Garrett, R. J. Beswick, T. W. B. Muxlow
arxiv-2103-08575.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. F. Radcliffe, P. D. Barthel, A. P. Thomson, M. A. Garrett, R. J. Beswick, T. W. B. Muxlow. Obtaining a census of active galactic nuclei (AGN) activity across cosmic time is critical to our understanding of galaxy evolution and formation. Many AGN classification techniques are compromised by dust obscuration.

arxiv-2107-07765.title: Piecewise strongly proximal actions, free boundaries and the Neretin groups
arxiv-2107-07765.creator: Pierre-Emmanuel Caprace, Adrien Le Boudec, Nicolás Matte Bon
arxiv-2107-07765.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pierre-Emmanuel Caprace, Adrien Le Boudec, Nicolás Matte Bon. A closed subgroup H H of a locally compact group G G is confined if the closure of the conjugacy class of H H in the Chabauty space of G G does not contain the trivial subgroup. We establish a dynamical criterion on the action of a totally disconnected locally compact group G G on a compact space X X ensuring that no relatively amenable subgroup of G G can be confined.

arxiv-2207-10403.title: Quantum graphs: Coulomb-type potentials and exactly solvable models
arxiv-2207-10403.creator: Yuriy Golovaty
arxiv-2207-10403.description: Abstract . We study the Schrödinger operators on a non-compact star graph with the Coulomb-type potentials having singularities at the vertex. The convergence of regularized Hamiltonians H ε H_{\varepsilon} with cut-off Coulomb potentials coupled with ( α ​ δ + β ​ δ ′ ) (\alpha\delta+\beta\delta^{\prime}) -like ones is investigated.

arxiv-2209-13967.title: Calibration-based abundances in the interstellar gas of galaxies from slit and IFU spectra
arxiv-2209-13967.creator: L. S. Pilyugin, M. A. Lara-López, J. M. Vílchez, S. Duarte Puertas, I. A. Zinchenko, O. L. Dors Jr
arxiv-2209-13967.description: Abstract In this work we make use of available Integral Field Unit (IFU) spectroscopy and slit spectra of several nearby galaxies. The pre-existing empirical R and S calibrations for abundance determinations are constructed using a sample of H ii regions with high quality slit spectra. In this paper, we test the applicability of those calibrations to the IFU spectra.

arxiv-2508-09571.title: Laser-induced topological phases in monolayer amorphous carbon
arxiv-2508-09571.creator: Arnob Kumar Ghosh, Quentin Marsal, Annica M. Black-Schaffer
arxiv-2508-09571.description: Abstract Driving non-topological materials out of equilibrium using time-periodic perturbations, such as circularly-polarized laser light, is a compelling way to engineer topological phases. At the same time, topology has traditionally only been considered for crystalline materials. Here we propose an experimentally feasible way of driving monolayer amorphous carbon topological.

pmc-10756913.title: Ultrasonic therapies for seizures and drug-resistant epilepsy
pmc-10756913.creator: Carena Cornelssen, Eli Finlinson, John D. Rolston, Karen S. Wilcox
pmc-10756913.description: Ultrasonic therapy is an increasingly promising approach for the treatment of seizures and drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Therapeutic focused ultrasound (FUS) uses thermal or nonthermal energy to either ablate neural tissue or modulate neural activity through high- or low-intensity FUS (HIFU, LIFU), respectively.

pmc-11616151.title: Symptomatic arachnoid cysts in adults: illustrative cases
pmc-11616151.creator: Hannah K Weiss, Emmajane G Rhodenhiser, David H Harter
pmc-11616151.description: BACKGROUNDAlthough intracranial arachnoid cysts are often asymptomatic, a small subset of patients develop debilitating symptoms. A cohort of patients with arachnoid cysts with varying presentations underwent endoscopic cystoventriculostomy, with a significant reduction in symptoms.OBSERVATIONSThree patients presented with chronic complaints, all involving headache in addition to other symptoms, and were noted to have large intracranial arachnoid cysts on imaging.

pmc-11677019.title: Arrhythmia Detection in Atrioventricular, Single-Lead, Floating Atrial Dipole ICD Systems Compared with Conventional Single- and Dual-Chamber Defibrillators
pmc-11677019.creator: Flora Diana Gausz, Kom Nangob Manuela Lena, Paul Emmanuel Gedeon, Marton Miklos, Attila Benak, Gabor Bencsik, Attila Makai, Dora Kranyak, Rita Beata Gagyi, Robert Pap, Laszlo Saghy, Tamas Szili-Torok, Mate Vamos, Michael Spartalis, Alexander H Maass
pmc-11677019.description: Background: An atrioventricular defibrillator system with a floating atrial dipole (VDD ICD) can provide atrial sensing by a single lead. Our aim was to compare the arrhythmia detection efficacy of VDD ICDs with conventional single- (VVI) and dual-chamber (DDD) defibrillators. Methods: Data from consecutive patients undergoing ICD implantation were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-11690081.title: OPTIMUM CIRCADIAN RHYTHM FOR HEALTHY LIFESPAN
pmc-11690081.creator: Satchidananda Panda
pmc-11690081.description: To thrive within nature day-night cycle, our genetic makeup is designed to orchestrate the rise and fall of nearly every gene in our genome at specific times. This rhythmic gene expression is vital for maintaining overall health and vitality. In our modern world, circadian rhythms are frequently disrupted, elevating risks of various chronic diseases.

pmc-12873744.title: Acid ceramidase expression and biomarker potential in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer
pmc-12873744.creator: Jasna Bjelanovic, Katarina Zeljic, Marko Miladinov, Goran Barisic, Sandra Dragicevic
pmc-12873744.description: Acid ceramidase (AC), a pivotal enzyme in sphingolipid metabolism, has been associated with various cancers; however, its specific role in rectal cancer remains poorly understood. This study aimed to explore the clinical significance of AC gene and protein expression in rectal cancer.

pmc-12982938.title: INPRESS: INvasive PRESSure Monitoring Knowledge and Practice Survey
pmc-12982938.creator: Oliver Coolens, Rolf Dubb, Arnold Kaltwasser, Ulf Lorenzen, Peter Nydahl
pmc-12982938.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn patients on Intensive Care Units (ICU), invasive arterial pressure monitoring with closed transducer systems is widely used, yet the accuracy of measurement depends on correct zeroing, levelling and interpretation of arterial waveforms.AimThe aim was to assess the knowledge and practice of clinicians (nurses, physicians, anaesthesia/operation technicians) working in critical care, operating theatres and emergency departments about arterial blood pressure assessment and managing the closed transducer system.Study DesignA cross‐sectional online survey was conducted in Germany in May 2025.

pmc-13091622.title: The Evolving Role of AI in Simulation-Based Medical Education: A Narrative Review
pmc-13091622.creator: Selina Hasan, Ayesha Ahmed, Faisal Wasim Ismail
pmc-13091622.description: PurposeA growing body of literature has emerged on the topic of Artificial Intelligence (AI) use in Simulation-Based Medical Education (SBME) in recent years, but most studies have focused on isolated applications of AI to components of simulation, making it difficult for educators and decision makers to make informed decisions on the use of AI.

pmc-13577629.title: Integrating soft skills into perfusion education: a necessity for modern clinical practice
pmc-13577629.creator: Salman Pervaiz Butt, Salman Abdulaziz, Umer Darr, Gopal Bhatnagar
pmc-13577629.description: Soft, non-technical competencies are important in perfusion practice but are often inconsistently taught. Key domains include communication, teamwork, leadership, adaptability, emotional intelligence, conflict management, professionalism, and cultural awareness. Suggested methods are interprofessional simulation, structured debriefing with feedback, short courses on communication and conflict resolution, mentored rotations with behavioral checklists, and recognition of progress through competency milestones and continuing professional development.

uslaw-usc-t14-s306.title: 14 U.S.C. § 306 — Retirement
uslaw-usc-t14-s306.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t14-s306.description: United States Code, Title 14 (Coast Guard); Chapter 3 (Composition And Organization); Subchapter II (Positions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) An officer, other than the Commandant or Vice Commandant, who, while serving in the grade of admiral or vice admiral, is retired for physical disability shall be placed on the retired list with the highest grade in which that officer served.

uslaw-usc-t36-s21008.title: 36 U.S.C. § 21008 — Duty to maintain corporate and tax-exempt status
uslaw-usc-t36-s21008.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s21008.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 210 (American Gi Forum Of The United States). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Corporate Status.— The corporation shall maintain its status as a corporation incorporated under the laws of Texas. (b) Tax-Exempt Status.— The corporation shall maintain its status as an organization exempt from taxation.
